take_homes: Licences handed out is not adoption. Absorption is the number that matters, and nobody reports it.
Before rolling anything out, ask the person doing the job what they use today and what would have to be true for them to switch.
A plan with unnamed owners is not a plan. Name who owns it, who governs it, and the first cheap test.

monday.move: Ask my controller how she does month-end variance commentary today, what she would need to see before she stopped doing it that way, and what one test would show it.
monday.stop_condition: She names no specific thing she would trust, or finance data is not cleared for the tool.
monday.blocker: IT has not approved the tool for finance data, and I still have no cost figure per user.

misconception.why: I still think of AI as a licence I buy. The point that access is a switch and absorption happens in people's weeks fits what I saw with our portal. I am not convinced it is a capability we build, since the module never gave me a cost or payback.

one_line: Decent point that rolling out a licence is not adoption, and the useful part came late, but I got no cost number and sat through seven paragraphs of filler.
